notes: SIGNUP PATH, read today. The account is created at https://signup.oraclecloud.com/ and nowhere else; oracle.com/cloud/free is the marketing page and signup.cloud.oracle.com serves the same shell. The page is a React application whose HTML carries no form, so the field list is taken from Oracle's own signup document, which walks the same form step by step. In order: country (some countries, Russia named, need the Terms accepted by checkbox), name, email, CAPTCHA, an email verification link valid 30 minutes, a password of 8-40 characters with upper, lower, digit and symbol, an optional company, a cloud account name, a home region that cannot be changed afterwards, the Terms, then address and phone number, then the card, then 'Start my free trial'. There is no identity document and no company requirement; the company field is explicitly optional. The home region matters more than the card: the client has no region in his own country and must pick an adjacent one, and the region cannot be changed, so a wrong pick is a new account. THE GRANT IS TWO PRODUCTS, not one. Always Free is the unlimited-period allowance described in free_tier.stated. The USD 300 is a separate 30-day trial that begins at the same signup and expires on its own; the FAQ says Always Free resources survive that expiry, but anything created with trial credit is reclaimed. So 'USD 300 for 90 days' is not what Oracle sells here: it is USD 300 for 30 days plus a permanent allowance. THE HOLD IS USD 1.00, published by Oracle's billing documentation, not by the signup page; the signup page says only 'a small, temporary charge' and names no amount. THE FAILURE MODE is the reason this row is a caveat and not a yes. Oracle refuses signups with a message that names three causes and no remedy, and two 2026 threads on Oracle's own forum show it arriving from Saudi Arabia and from a card that had just verified successfully. The country page says the tier is available wherever commercial OCI runs; there is no OCI region in Viet Nam, Thailand, Indonesia or the Philippines, so a client in one of those picks an adjacent region, and Oracle's fraud checks read the mismatch between the declared address and the connection. That is reported, not documented: nobody publishes the rule. What I could not establish: whether a signup from any particular country succeeds, because that requires making an account and I did not; and the true minimum boot volume, because the page states 47 GB and 50 GB in two paragraphs.
